pr.title: Only traverse reachable blocks in JumpThreading.
pr.description:
Fixes https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/131451

We only compute loop headers for reachable blocks. We shouldn't try to perform an opt on unreachable blocks anyway.

pr.author: cjgillot

processing.reason: The PR changes only the candidate-block iteration of JumpThreading from `body.basic_blocks.indices()` to `traversal::preorder(body)`. The historical misbehavior is attempting the pass on unreachable CFG blocks for which loop-header information was not computed, producing a compile-time crash; the regression is a `//@ build-pass` UI test with no execution. The diff contains no source-level value assignment or expression rewrite, so there is no historically justified original/transformed Rust function pair that can differ on concrete inputs under Miri. Any such value difference would be a fabricated, unrelated rewrite rather than a reconstruction of this patch's semantics.

analysis.summary: JumpThreading must seed its switch-threading search only from reachable MIR basic blocks. The historical implementation iterated over every index in `body.basic_blocks`, including unreachable blocks, even though loop headers are computed only for reachable blocks, so it attempted an optimization on blocks it could not safely analyze. The fix iterates in `traversal::preorder(body)` order and turns the prior crash regression into a `build-pass` UI test.
analysis.originalLogic: JumpThreading collected threading opportunities by starting from every basic block index: `for bb in body.basic_blocks.indices() { finder.start_from_switch(bb); }`. That treats all allocated basic blocks as candidates, regardless of CFG reachability.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The pass attempted to perform JumpThreading's switch analysis, via `finder.start_from_switch(bb)`, on unreachable basic blocks as well as reachable ones. This is the historically incorrect behavior: it fed unreachable blocks into an optimization whose supporting loop-header information exists only for reachable blocks. The corrected behavior restricts candidates to blocks yielded by `traversal::preorder(body)`. Note: the patch does not show a specific MIR value rewrite; the incorrect action is the attempted optimization over unreachable blocks that triggers a crash.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies containing unreachable basic blocks, particularly code after an unconditional infinite loop such as `while true {}` followed by another loop. The supplied regression program is: `pub fn fun(terminate: bool) { while true {} while !terminate {} }`, compiled as a library with `-Zmir-enable-passes=+GVN -Zmir-enable-passes=+JumpThreading`.
analysis.trigger: JumpThreading processes an unreachable block in `body.basic_blocks`, for which no loop header was computed, because the pass iterates over all block indices instead of only CFG-reachable blocks.
preconditions: The compiled MIR contains at least one unreachable basic block.
JumpThreading is enabled, for example via `-Zmir-enable-passes=+JumpThreading`.
The historical test also enables GVN (`-Zmir-enable-passes=+GVN`) and requires debug assertions (`//@ needs-rustc-debug-assertions`).
pitfalls: Do not assume every index in `body.basic_blocks` is reachable; unreachable blocks can remain in the MIR body.
Loop-header analysis is only available for reachable blocks, so JumpThreading must not start analysis from unreachable blocks.
The regression changed from a known-bug crash test to `//@ build-pass`; it is not evidence of a runtime behavior test or of executing the compiled function.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a UI/regression test with a function whose first statement is an unconditional infinite loop (`while true {}`) followed by a second loop, compile it with `-Zmir-enable-passes=+GVN -Zmir-enable-passes=+JumpThreading --crate-type=lib`, require `//@ needs-rustc-debug-assertions`, and mark it `//@ build-pass`. Update the expected stderr for the `while_true` lint (`warning: denote infinite loops with `loop { ... }``) so the test checks successful compilation rather than a crash. No compiler was built and no execution/reproduction is claimed here.
evidence: Only traverse reachable blocks in JumpThreading.
We only compute loop headers for reachable blocks. We shouldn't try to perform an opt on unreachable blocks anyway.
